sourceReview.scope: Formal opening speeches, both rebuttal rounds and both closings only; moderator logistics, breaks and audience Q&A excluded.
findings: Every card was directly reviewed against its inventory source and resolved judgment before exact-byte submission; nine authorized source/clarity leaves corrected in the same unsaved context.
Nugent moral realism, fallible atheism, revised causal concession, incomplete emergence mechanism and internal moral objections retained.
Craig neutral fine-tuning definition, theorem-versus-boundary distinctions, logical-versus-probabilistic evil response, personal warrant and rational-defeater qualification retained.
Nugent final-closing resurrection response imposes no failure-to-reply penalty on Craig, who had no subsequent formal speech.
sourceReview.quotationCompleteness: Both exact excerpts assert complete propositions without relying on their contexts to finish an argument; Craig distinguishes definition from inference and Nugent makes a comparative evidential challenge.

findings: The pro modal-ground argument tests explanatory unity and divine necessity; its cognition argument introduces abstract rational reliability. The con prediction argument tests antecedent expectations; its access argument tests geographic and cultural distribution. These are distinct contributions.

Theses lead with cumulative worldview claims, premises develop domain-specific conditions and conclusions retain defeasible comparative qualifications. The common conditional inference is philosophically relevant rather than a recycled prose scaffold.

Direct prose retains commas in lists, introductory clauses and qualifications, colon-led consequence, semicolon-free natural sentences, and terminal punctuation. No text announces its own provenance inside the already disclosed AI section.
Exchanging side labels or titles would break the specific modal, cognitive, predictive and epistemic inferences; overlapping short expressions, if any, do not supply an interchangeable argument.
